messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-98123 fired -> routing-proxy-us-west1 5xx spike (threshold: 2% over 30s)
jamie: Acked. I'll take primary.
lee: seeing the pager, no customer slack tickets yet. pulling metrics.
sasha: Grafana shows a short 503 spike from 13:02:07 -> 13:03:30 UTC on routing-proxy-us-west1, peaked ~4.6%.
jamie: checking logs now, grep for 503s across proxies. running:
```bash
$ k logs -l app=routing-proxy -n prod --since=5m | grep "HTTP/1.1" | grep 503 | head -n 20
```
jamie: logs show rapid 503 responses with upstream rc=ECONNRESET on a handful of envoy workers. sample: `upstream_reset: connection failure`
morgan: checking autoscaler events, no scale up/down around that time. host health checks looked ok.
lee: product-side synthetic canaries reported a single failed check aligned to the spike, then recovered. no broad customer impact in frontend error-tracking.
sasha: quick snapshot of request volume — traffic stayed stable, request latency normal. suggests transient upstream flake rather than sustained overload.
jamie: incident-bot shows pager auto-resolved at 13:03:40 UTC (PD auto-close). I'm going to run a quick curl against the proxy to sanity check endpoints:
```bash
$ curl -I https://routing-proxy-us-west1.redwood.internal/healthz
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
jamie: health is green. I'm going to mark this as no-customer-impact and leave a follow-up. creating ticket now: INFRA-1456 (short postmortem + logs).
morgan: +1 on follow-up. suggest we add a short-term alert tweak: require 2 consecutive 30s windows before paging to reduce noise for ephemeral upstream resets.
sasha: agree. also add a synthetic canary check that hits a pinned backend to detect upstream resets quicker.
lee: did we get any PagerDuty escalations?
jamie: no escalations, only the initial page and an auto-resolve. pager history: PD-98123 fired -> ack by jamie -> auto-resolve.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-98123 auto-resolved by PD policy (no-overtime).
morgan: quick risk note — if we see repeated 5xx blips across regions, escalate to routing-runtime. for now, low severity.
jamie: i'll leave the ticket with attached logs and timeline, assign to eng-runtime for a look in the morning. shifting oncall to morgan in 10m, FYI. :thumbsup:
morgan: taking handoff. thanks. I'll watch for recurrence during my shift.
lee: tagging support so they can message customers proactively if anything changes: @support-team
jamie: thanks team — closing thread.
_meta: generated for dataset: realistic eng-oncall thread about flapping automated pager that auto-resolved; includes incident-bot messages, ack, quick triage, follow-up ticket creation
